description: This program-core course, offered by the Department of Electrical Engineering, aims to help students acquire the basic knowledge of analog and digital logic levels and apply that knowledge to understand analog and digital electronic circuits. It also prepares students to perform the analysis and design of various analog and digital electronic circuits.

syllabus.title: BJT Biasing
syllabus.body: DC biasing: voltage divider bias, self bias, emitter bias. AC biasing, re model. Amplifiers: Class A, Class B, Class C and Class D, push-pull amplifier.

syllabus.title: OP-AMP
syllabus.body: OP-AMP characteristics, non-inverting / inverting amplifier, linear and non-linear OP-AMP circuits, regulated power supplies. Oscillators: Barkhausen criteria of oscillations, Wein-bridge oscillator, RC oscillator.

syllabus.title: Digital Logic and Combinational / Sequential Circuits
syllabus.body: Number system, logic gates, K-map reduction techniques, introduction to combinational circuits, design of half adder and full adder, introduction to sequential circuits, flip-flops (RS, JK, D and T).

syllabus.title: Timers, Converters and Filters
syllabus.body: 555 timer: its monostable and astable operation, Schmitt triggers, sample and hold circuits, A/D and D/A converters, low pass filter, high pass filter, counter and register, case study of simulation circuits.

outcomes: Have a thorough understanding of the fundamental concepts and techniques used in analog and digital electronics.
Understand and examine the structure of various number systems and their application in digital design.
Understand, analyze and design various combinational and sequential circuits.
Develop the skill to build and troubleshoot analog and digital circuits.
textbooks: Millman and Halkias, Integrated Electronics, McGraw Hill, 2nd Edition, 2017.
R. Boylestad and L. Nashelsky, Electronic Devices and Circuits, Prentice Hall India, 10th Edition, 2009.
Millman and Halkias, Electronic Devices and Circuits, TMH, 4th Edition, 2015.
referenceBooks: Malcolm Goodge, Analog Electronics: Analysis and Synthesis, TMH Edition.
A. P. Malvino and D. P. Leach, Digital Principles and Applications, TMH, 8th Edition, 2014.
Charles Roth, Fundamentals of Logic Design, Wadsworth Publishing, 5th Edition, 2005.
